correctness.rationale: Each averaging step nests the convex hull. On a periodic orbit every hull is identical. Extreme-vertex labels can only persist, never appear from the interior because self-weights are positive; periodicity forces their sets to be constant. For n<=3 this leaves either all agents fixed or one mobile agent between fixed endpoints. Star-shaped radial membership makes left trust nonincreasing and right trust nondecreasing in the mobile scalar coordinate; explicit rational formulas show the resulting map is nondecreasing. No nondecreasing one-dimensional map has a nonfixed finite cycle. For n=4 the explicit closed star-shaped disk-and-rays confidence set gives the exact 2-step itinerary 0->2->0 and all three anchors frozen; stand-alone exact-rational checker passed 2925 order comparisons and both neighbor-set calculations. No computational enumeration substitutes for the infinite-domain proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 source proves symmetry-based convergence, and illustrates three-agent nonstar-shaped and four-agent star-shaped cycles, without establishing minimality. Scalar asymmetric HK convergence theorems do not imply that a vector-valued three-agent periodic orbit has a fixed segment hull. The new vertex-persistence reduction establishes this missing universal lower bound. Indexed and accessible historical comparisons yielded no implication-covering statement; novelty remains a qualified, not exhaustive, literature conclusion.
residual_risks: The 2022 specialist full theorem appendices were not directly inspected; the accessible scope and 2024 survey restrict their stated result to scalar intervals.
An unindexed equivalent three-agent convex-hull reduction might exist; absence from indexed results does not establish universal novelty.
The claim does not extend to heterogeneous confidence or to externally stubborn agents; those models have documented three-agent cycles.

value.rationale: The paper studies periodic social-opinion behavior made possible by unusual confidence geometry and provides a four-agent star-shaped witness; its minimal required social-group size was unresolved by the provided examples. The new global theorem proves exactly n=4 is the first possible size, ruling out every finite period for all star-shaped sets in any finite dimension with n<=3. Sharp small-population thresholds are intrinsically motivated structural information for such agent models, distinguish radial holes from nonconvexity, and are not routine parameter increments or computed table entries.
